finding.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
finding.summary: AvatarStorage allowlists image/svg+xml by detected content type and stores the bytes unchanged (no re-encoding). AvatarDownloadController then serves a stored .svg back with Content-Type image/svg+xml and no Content-Disposition/nosniff header, so a browser navigating to the URL renders any <script> the uploaded SVG carries in the application's origin.

trap: Adding a Content-Disposition: attachment header forces a download prompt for a browser navigating directly to the URL, but does not fix a caller that fetches the bytes through an , an API client, or any other path that renders the response body inline - an SVG containing a
must_preserve: Uploaded PNG and JPEG avatars are still stored and served back unchanged. An avatar stored under a name returned by AvatarStorage.store() is still retrievable at GET /api/avatars/{storedName}.
